examples.en: We signed a contract with the client.

examples.sr: Наш [до̏гово̄р] је био да поделимо трошкове.
examples.en: Our agreement was to split the costs.

related.en: contract — a written document: employment, lease, with a client
agreement, arrangement — made in words between people

meanings: how to say «to meet»: састати се, срести, наићи, дочекати

examples.en: We often meet after work.
Yesterday I ran into my neighbor on the stairs.

examples.sr: Јуче сам [на̀ишао] на њу у продавници.
examples.en: Yesterday I came across her at the store.
We rang in the New Year with our family.

related.en: to meet (by arrangement) — a planned business or friendly meeting
to meet, to run into — the general verb: planned and chance meetings alike
to come across, to run into — to meet by chance
to welcome, to see in — guests, a holiday, an event

note: After наи́ћи always comes на + acc.: наи́ћи на њу̑.

meanings: how to say «to call»: звонити, позвати, јавити се, телефонирати

examples.en: The phone is ringing.
Call me tomorrow at eight o'clock.
I'll get in touch with you tomorrow.
She phones her mother every evening.

related.en: to ring — only when a bell or phone rings: «Телефон звони»
to call (someone) — the basic verb for phoning a person
to get in touch, to call back — broader: to contact, to answer a call
to phone, to call — biaspectual, neutral, slightly bookish

note: По̀звати also means «to invite»: позвали су ме на рођендан. And ја́вити се also means «to answer the phone»: јави се на телефон.

examples.en: Here is the school timetable.
Look at the train timetable.
The festival schedule has been published.

related.en: schedule (general) — classes, work, meetings, duties
timetable — buses, trams, trains
hour-by-hour schedule — a conference, a festival, a working day

note: For flights, ре̑д ле́то̄ва̄ is used, not ред вожње.

meanings: how to say goodbye: довиђења, ћао, збогом, видимо се

examples.en: Goodbye, Director!
Bye, see you tomorrow!
Farewell, and thanks for everything.
See you on Friday!

related.en: goodbye — neutral and polite: with colleagues, people you barely know
bye, hi — with people you are on first-name terms with
farewell — solemn, formal or dramatic
see you — to friends, when you will meet soon

note: Ћа̑о is said both when meeting and when parting. There is also чу̏је̄мо се - «we'll talk» (by phone).

meanings: words for a dog: пас, псето, куче, штене, кер, џукела

examples.en: I've had a dog for five years.
Look at that little doggy!
Get that mutt away from me!
What a cute little dog!

examples.sr: Наше [штѐне] још учи да хода на поводцу.
examples.en: Our puppy is still learning to walk on a leash.
Some mutt barked all night.
Careful, that cur bites!

related.en: dog — the neutral word
doggy, little dog — diminutive, often a puppy too
mutt — contemptuous
doggie, pooch — affectionate, also for a grown dog
puppy — a young dog
cur, stray — rude
cur, mongrel — rude; also used of a nasty person

note:
How to choose:
• neutral - па̏с
• affectionate - пси̏ћ, ку̏че
• rude - псе̏то, ке̑р, џу̀кела
• a young dog - штѐне

examples.sr: Тешко ми је [одлу́чити] шта да обучем.
examples.en: It's hard for me to decide what to wear.
We have to solve this problem.

related.en: to decide, to make a decision — to choose, to make a choice
to solve — first of all to resolve a problem or a task

note: «To solve a problem» is only ре́шити: ре́шити зада́так. «To make a decision» is одлу́чити or донети одлуку.

meanings: how to say «to go» by vehicle: ићи, возити се, путовати

examples.en: I'm going home by bus.
I like riding my bike.
We're going to Montenegro by train.

related.en: to go (on foot or by vehicle) — the simplest option
to ride, to go for a ride — on transport, often regularly or for pleasure
to travel, to be on the way — a trip or a journey

note: Ѝћи means both «to go on foot» and «to go by vehicle». «To drive a car» is во̀зити without се: возим аутомобил.

examples.en: This year we're spending the summer at the seaside.
They are flying to Podgorica.

related.en: to spend the summer, to vacation in summer
to fly — to move through the air

note: Лѐтовати is about the summer, not about flying. The two verbs conjugate differently: летујем, but лѐтӣм.

examples.en: We have a small house in the countryside.

examples.sr: Живимо у новој [згра̏ди] на Новом Београду.
examples.en: We live in a new apartment building in New Belgrade.
Welcome to my home!

related.en: house — a detached house of one or two floors
building, apartment block — a multistory building
home, hearth — one's own home; in names of institutions: дом здравља - health center, студентски дом - dormitory

note: Ко̏д ку̏ће means «at home» wherever you live: in a ку̏ћа or in a згра̏да.

examples.en: I study Serbian every day.
She is getting her education in Belgrade.
I'm studying medicine in Belgrade.

related.en: to learn, to study — the most general word
to be educated, to go to school — over several years: school, college, university
to study at university — to study a particular field

note: A schoolchild does not студира: he иде у школу or учи.

examples.sr: Влада је уложила много [но́вца] у пројекат.
examples.en: The government invested a lot of money in the project.
I don't have enough money to buy it.

related.en: money — neutral and official; singular only
money — colloquial; plural only, from Turkish

note: Genitive: нема новца, нема пара. Па̏ра in the singular means «steam»: пара из чајника.

meanings: how to say «to gather, to collect»: скупљати, окупљати, склапати, брати, паковати

examples.en: I collect postcards from different countries.
We're collecting signatures for the petition.
We get together with friends at the café.
He's been putting the wardrobe together for two hours.
We picked mushrooms in the forest.
I'm still packing my suitcase for the trip.

related.en: to collect, to gather — data, things, people, a collection
to gather people — only of people; окупљати се - to get together
to assemble — from parts: furniture, a model kit; close to састављати
to pick — to harvest: mushrooms, flowers, fruit
to pack — things, luggage for a trip

note: Serbian uses a different verb for each kind of object: people, parts, harvest or things for a trip.

examples.en: Every morning we go out for a run.
He always runs away from problems.

related.en: to run — physical running: sport, a jog, hurrying
to flee, to run away — also figuratively: to run from problems

examples.sr: Сутра морам да [сре̏дим] овај хаос у ормару.
examples.en: Tomorrow I have to sort out this mess in the wardrobe.
The trip threw off my daily routine.

related.en: to put in order, to sort out — things, papers, thoughts
to disrupt, to upset — order, routine, plans

note: Imperfective forms: сређи́вати and рѐметити.

meanings: verbs of payment: платити, уплатити, исплатити, наплатити

examples.en: Can I pay by card?
Yesterday I paid the loan installment.
The bank will pay the owner a dividend.
The taxi driver charged me four thousand.

related.en: to pay — to pay for a purchase or a bill
to pay in, to transfer — money into an account or toward a payment
to pay out — to hand over a sum: salary, dividends
to charge, to collect payment — said of the one who receives the money: a taxi driver, a seller

note: Nouns: у̀плата (payment in) and и̏сплата (payout). На̀платити also means «to collect (a debt)»: на̀платити ду̏г.

meanings: how to say «to hurt, to be ill»: болети, бити болестан, боловати

examples.en: My throat hurts.
My cat is sick.
He suffers from a serious illness.

related.en: to hurt, to ache (of a body part)
to be ill — the state right now
to be ill for a long time — a serious illness; «боловати од» + gen.

note: With бо̀лети the sore spot is the subject and the person is in the acc.: боли ме грло, бо̑ле ме ле́ђа.

meanings: how to say «tour, excursion»: обилазак, тура, излет, екскурзија

examples.en: The tour of the fortress lasted two hours.

examples.sr: Водич нас је повео на [ту̏ру] по старом граду.
examples.en: The guide took us on a tour of the old town.
We organize trips to Montenegro.
The pupils are going on a school trip.

related.en: sightseeing visit, tour — a visit to a place or to sights
short guided tour — brief, with a guide
outing, day trip — a trip to the countryside: picnic, walk, a trip to another town
organized trip — for a group, more often a school one

note: A sightseeing tour of a city is an оби́лазак or ту̑ра, not an екску̀рзија.

meanings: how to say «owner, landlord, host»: власник, станодавац, газда, домаћин

examples.en: Who is the owner of this dog?
The landlord comes for the rent every month.
The owner closed the café.
The host offered the guests rakija.

related.en: owner — a broad word: legal and colloquial
landlord — the one who rents out housing
boss, owner — informal: the owner of a café, a workshop
host — the master of the house, who receives guests

note: A landlord of a rented apartment is a станода̀вац: вла̑снӣк is closer to «owner». Female forms: вла̑сница, станодавка, дома̀ћица.

meanings: how to say «shade, shadow»: хлад, хладовина, сенка

examples.en: We took shelter in the shade.
It's really hot, let's go into the shade!
There is the shadow of a tree on the wall.

related.en: shade, coolness — shelter from the heat
shade, a cool spot — a shady corner
shadow (silhouette) — the shadow cast by an object

note: Се̑нка is also used figuratively: сенка сумње - «a shadow of a doubt».

meanings: words for heat: врућина, жега, спарина, припека

examples.en: It's really hot today.
The heat is unbearable.
The muggy heat is awful.
Don't go out into the blazing sun without a hat.

related.en: heat — the general word
scorching heat — intense heat
muggy heat — hot and humid
blazing sun — direct sunshine

note: Спа̀рина has a synonym: оморина.

meanings: to get a tan: сунчати се, поцрнети, препланути, добити боју

examples.en: We spend all day sunbathing on the beach.
Everyone got a tan at the seaside.

examples.sr: Ако не желите да [до̀бијете бо̀ју], користите крему.
examples.en: If you don't want to get a tan, use sunscreen.

examples.sr: Ја сам [препла̀нула] јер сам била на мору.
examples.en: I'm tanned because I was at the seaside.

related.en: to sunbathe (the process) — to lie in the sun
to get tanned — literally «to turn black»
to get a tan — literally «to get color»
to be tanned — the result

note: A tanned person: препланео (m.), препланула (f.). Су̀нчати се is the process, the others the result.

examples.en: Well, I don't know.
Come on, how should I know!
Oh, come on! I don't believe it!

related.en: well, so, because — links replies, explains, continues a thought
oh come on, no way — emotional: disbelief, irritation, brushing something off

note: Па softly opens a reply: па до̀бро - «well, all right». Ма̏ is sharper: ма̏ јо̏к! - «no way!»

examples.en: Life is beautiful.
My stomach hurts.
Sweets make my belly grow.

related.en: life — not a part of the body
stomach, tummy — when it hurts after eating
belly, paunch — the outer belly

note: «My stomach hurts» is боли ме стомак, not жѝвот, which is «life».

examples.en: I've done only one task, nothing more.
I've done just one task so far, and I'll continue.
It worked only on the fifth attempt.

related.en: only — a limit: nothing more, a total
only, just, not until — the start of a process or a late moment; «тек сад» - «only now»

note: Са̏мо што̏ also means «just now»: само што је стигао - «he has only just arrived».

meanings: come on, let's, don't: ајде, ајмо, немој, немојмо

examples.en: Come on, get out of here!
Let's go to the gym!
Don't be late.
Let's not argue.

related.en: come on, go on — urging the listener
let's go — a suggestion to do something together
don't — a prohibition; -те for the polite form and the plural
let's not — giving up an action together with the speaker

note: А̀јде and не̏мој address the listener, а̀јмо and не̏мојмо include the speaker. After не̏мој comes да + present or the infinitive: не̏мој да пи̑ше̄ш, не̏мој пи́сати - «don't write».

examples.en: I always pay by card.
I'm crying with happiness!

related.en: to pay — плаћам, плаћаш, плаћа
to cry — плачем, плачеш, плаче (к changes to ч)

note: Плаћам is with money, плачем is with tears.

examples.en: I put a spoonful of sour cream in the soup.
There's some mileram in the fridge.
Buy sweet cream for the cake.

related.en: sour cream — the basic option
thick sour cream — a bit richer, sold as a separate product
cream — without «кисела»

note: Whipping cream is слатка павлака.

examples.sr: Већ три месеца [ре̏до̄вно] идем на пливање.
examples.en: I've been going swimming regularly for three months now.
I don't have regular working hours.

related.en: regular, steady — happens in order: habits, visitors
proper, normal, by the rules — meets the norm

note: The regular price, without a discount, is редовна цена.

meanings: to understand: разумети, схватити, сконтати, скапирати

examples.en: I didn't understand you very well.

examples.sr: Коначно сам [схва̀тио] у чему је проблем.
examples.en: I finally figured out what the problem is.

examples.sr: Коначно сам [ско̀нтао] како ради ова апликација.
examples.en: I finally got how this app works.
I realized right away that it was a trap.

related.en: to understand — neutral, formal
to grasp — to catch the point quickly, mostly in the past
to figure out — colloquial, after some thought
to get it, to catch on — colloquial, everyday speech, a sudden realization

note: The colloquial «got it?» is капираш? (from скапѝрати).

examples.en: Add one tablespoon of flour.
Put a teaspoon of sugar in the coffee.

related.en: tablespoon — for flour, juice, sauce
teaspoon — for sugar, salt, spices

note: The spoons are named after the dishes: супена - for soup, кафена - for coffee. Plain ка̀шика is a spoon in general.

examples.sr: [По̀следњӣ] филм који сам гледао био је добар.
examples.en: The last movie I watched was good.
The final deadline is Friday.

related.en: last — at the end of a series: the last film, the last task
final, ultimate — at the very edge or limit: the final deadline, the last stop

note: «Last» meaning «previous» is not по̀следњӣ: прошле недеље - «last week».

examples.sr: Моје [ми̏шље̄ње] је да је филм одличан.
examples.en: My opinion is that the film is excellent.
Thinking about the future motivates me.

related.en: opinion — the result of thinking, a position
thinking, reflection — the process of pondering

note: The verbs are ми̏слити and разми́шљати. «In my opinion» is по мом мишљењу.

examples.en: The road is temporarily closed.
He's busy at the moment.

related.en: temporarily — for a limited time: «привремено затворен»
at the moment, currently — «тренутно радим»

note: The adjective is прѝвремен: прѝвременӣ по̀сао - «a temporary job».

meanings: to make, to do: правити, радити, чинити

examples.en: I'm making a cake for the birthday.
I'm doing my homework.
You're doing a good deed.

related.en: to make, to create — material things: a cake, noise
to do, to work — work and activities
to do, to commit — deeds and abstract things

note: «What are you doing?» is шта радиш?. Пра̏вити се means «to pretend»: прави се да не зна.

meanings: to know, to be able to: знати, умети, моћи

examples.en: I know where the store is.
I can cook.
I can come tomorrow.

related.en: to know — facts, information
to know how to — a skill, an ability
can, to be able to — possibility, permission

note: «To know how to swim» can be умем да пливам or знам да пливам.

examples.en: He drank as many as three glasses of wine.
I need at least five minutes.

related.en: even, as many as — emphasis, more than expected
at least — a minimum, the lower limit

note: Ча̏к и - «even»: ча̏к и дѐца зна̏јӯ - «even children know».

examples.en: I'm renting a furnished apartment.
I'm renting out a furnished apartment.

related.en: to rent (as a tenant), to hire — the one who pays
to rent out, to let — the owner, the one who lets it

note: Изна́јмити sometimes means «to rent out» too, so only издајем is unambiguously «I rent out». «To rent» can also be узети под кирију.

meanings: to flirt, to hang around: мувати, мувати се, смувати се

examples.en: Luka is hitting on the waitress.
He's always hanging around the house.

examples.sr: Милош и Маја су се [сму̀вали] прошлог лета.
examples.en: Miloš and Maja got together last summer.

related.en: to hit on, to flirt with someone
to hang around, to wander aimlessly
to start going out — the moment a relationship begins

note: Милош и Маја се мувају means that they are flirting with each other.

meanings: also, the same, similar: такође, исто, слично

examples.en: Marko is coming, and Ana too.
We have the same opinion.
This city is similar to Belgrade.

related.en: also, too — adds something similar
the same — stresses identity
similar, alike — resemblance without identity

note: И̏сто ми је - «I don't care».

examples.en: New textbooks are needed.
You should study every day.

related.en: needed, necessary — the stress is on things: «потребно је време» - «time is needed»
need to, should — the stress is on an action: «треба да учиш» - «you should study»

note: Тре́ба ми + nominative also means «I need»: тре́ба ми по̏мо̄ћ - «I need help».

examples.en: The next step is to fill out the form.
We're planning the project for the coming weeks.

related.en: next — neutral, everyday speech
next, upcoming — more formal, mostly about plans and deadlines

note: Слѐде̄ћӣ is also «next in line»: слѐде̄ћӣ, мо̏лим! - «next, please!»

meanings: to remember, to forget: сећати се, сетити се, заборавити

examples.sr: [Се̏ћам се] свог првог дана у школи.
examples.en: I remember my first day at school.

examples.sr: [Сѐтио сам се] да сам заборавио кључ.
examples.en: I remembered that I had forgotten the key.
I forgot where I left my phone.

related.en: to remember (impf.) — to have something in memory: «сећам се свог првог дана у школи»
to recall, to think of (pf.) — «сетио сам се да...»
to forget (pf.)

note: Се̏ћати се and се̏тити се take the genitive: сећам се њега. Забо̀равити takes the accusative: заборавио сам кључ.

examples.en: I agree with you.
I'm putting the T-shirts in the closet.
I lied to him.

related.en: to agree — always with «се»: «слажем се» - «I agree»
to put away, to stack — without «се» + accusative: «слажем дрва» - «I stack the firewood»
to lie, to tell a lie (pf.) — perfective of «лагати»: «слагао сам га» - «I lied to him»

note: «I agree» is always слажем се: without се it is a different verb, e.g. слажем мајице - «I fold T-shirts».

examples.en: I know where the library is.
I found out where the library is.

related.en: to know (impf.) — to have the information
to find out, to learn (pf.) — to get new information

note: «To recognize» is препо̀знати: нисам га препознао - «I didn't recognize him».

examples.en: I remember my childhood.
I remembered her name.

related.en: to remember (impf.) — memory in general
to recall, to think of (pf.) — a flash of memory at a specific moment

note: Both take the genitive: сећам се детињства, сетио сам се имена.

examples.en: I keep old photographs.
I saved all the messages.

related.en: to keep, to look after, to guard (impf.) — the process
to save, to preserve (pf.) — the result

note: Чу́вати де̏цу - «to look after children». Чувај се! - «take care of yourself».

examples.en: I'm starting to learn Serbian.

examples.sr: [По̀чео] сам да учим српски прошле године.
examples.en: I started learning Serbian last year.

related.en: to begin (impf.) — a process or a regular action
to begin (pf.) — a specific moment

note: Both also mean «to start» without се: филм почиње у осам - «the film starts at eight».

examples.en: Tell me what you think.
I think that you're right.
We know that you were here.

related.en: what (question word) — in direct and indirect questions: «шта хоћеш?», «не разумем шта кажеш»
that (conjunction) — joins two clauses: «мислим да си у праву»

note: Unlike English «that», да cannot be left out: мислим да сте у праву.

key: cmp:за + вин. п.-кроз + вин. п.-преко + род. п.
meanings: across, through, in: преко + gen., кроз + acc., за + acc.

examples.en: I'm crossing the bridge.
We went through the forest.
The train arrives in ten minutes.

related.en: across, over (a surface, an obstacle) — a street, a bridge: «прећи преко улице»
through (inside something) — a forest, a crowd, an opening: «проћи кроз шуму»
in (of time) — after a period of time: «за годину дана» - «in a year»

note: Пре̏ко is also used figuratively: преко интернета - «over the internet», преко пријатеља - «through friends».

meanings: to manage, to make it: успети, стићи

examples.en: I didn't manage to finish my homework.
I managed to solve the problem.
Will you make it to the train?

related.en: to manage, to succeed — it worked out: «успео сам да решим» (impf. успе́вати)
to make it in time; to arrive; to catch up (impf. сти̏зати)

note: Trap: «to make the train» is сти̏ћи на во̑з, not успети. У̀спети is about success: успео сам у животу - «I've succeeded in life».

examples.en: What are you doing?

examples.sr: Не могу да идем [за̀то̄ што̏] имам обавезе.
examples.en: I can't go because I have things to do.
That's the reason I didn't come.

related.en: what (question word) — in a question and an indirect question: «шта радиш?», «не знам шта да радим»
because, that (conjunction) — a reason: «зато што», «разлог што»

note: Што̏ is also «that» after све̏, оно: све̏ што̏ зна̑м. Colloquially it can mean «why»: што плачеш?

examples.en: I found money on the street by chance.
I finally found a job!
The police found the stolen car.

related.en: to find — to discover, also by chance: «морам да нађем кључ»
to find after effort — a long search, a valuable find

note: На́ћи се also means «to meet»: нађимо се у осам - «let's meet at eight».

examples.en: Last night I dreamed that I was flying.
He dreams of becoming a doctor.
I dream of a house by the sea.

related.en: to dream (in sleep); to dream of a goal — dreams in sleep are only сањати
to daydream, to fantasize — pleasant thoughts, real or not

meanings: to say, to speak, to talk: казати, рећи, причати, разговарати, говорити

examples.sr: Он [ка̏же] да те је срео јуче.
examples.en: He says that he met you yesterday.
I said everything I knew.
People are talking about you.
I need to talk to you.
He speaks three languages fluently.

related.en: to say, to tell — has a present tense: «он каже да...»
to say, to tell — perfective only: «рекла сам», «реците»
to tell, to chat, to talk — everyday, informal
to talk, to converse — a serious conversation with someone
to speak, to express oneself, to know a language

note: Ре̏ћи has no present tense, ка́зати takes its place: он каже - «he says», but он је рекао - «he said».

meanings: flower, flowers, blossoms: цвет, цвеће, цветови

examples.en: I have one flower in a pot.
I like planting flowers in the garden.
The first blossoms have opened on the tree.

related.en: a flower — a single one: «имам један цвет у саксији»
flowers (collective) — flowers in general, a bouquet, a flower bed
blossoms, individual flowers — on a tree or a stem, when the number matters

note: Цве̑ће is neuter singular: цве̑ће је ле̑по - «flowers are beautiful».

examples.sr: Дао ми је [на̑знаку] да му се свиђам.
examples.en: He gave me a hint that he likes me.
His look was a sign of trouble.

examples.sr: Изјава је била [а̀лӯзија] на прошли догађај.
examples.en: The statement was an allusion to a past event.

related.en: hint, sign — the closest to «a hint»
warning sign, veiled signal — foreshadows something: «наговештај невоље»
allusion — a cultural or ironic reference to an event or topic

note: Verbs: нагове́стити (impf. наговешта́вати), алуди́рати.

examples.en: I can't hear you, the microphone is off.

examples.sr: Волим да [слу̀шам] аудио књиге у превозу.
examples.en: I like listening to audiobooks on public transport.
He never listened to his parents' advice.

related.en: to hear — to perceive a sound without special attention: «не чујем те»
to listen — attentively, with concentration; also «to obey»

note: Чу̏ти за - «to hear of someone»: чуо сам за њега. Чу̏ти се - «to be in touch (by phone)».

examples.en: I go to work every day.
He went home.
I got home.

related.en: to go, to walk — movement in progress or a habit: «идем у школу»
to leave, to go away — left a place and is no longer there: «отишао је кући»
to come, to arrive — arrival at a destination: «дошао сам кући»

note: Оти́ћи and до́ћи have no present tense for «I'm leaving» and «I'm coming»: it is одлазим and долазим.

examples.en: You should get some rest.
I have to go.
I don't have to work today.

related.en: should, ought to — advice, a recommendation or an outside necessity: «треба да учим»
must, have to — a personal obligation: «морам да идем»

note: With a negation the meaning splits: не мо̑ра̄м да - «I don't have to», не тре́ба да - «I shouldn't».
